concerns.text: The `artifact_hash` field contains a placeholder value. Replace it with the actual SHA‑256 hash of the spec file's bytes to satisfy the review contract.

FR-004 specifies outlier removal using a Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) rule (|value – median| > 3.5 × MAD), while the Edge Cases section describes outlier removal as (±3 σ). These two definitions conflict, creating ambiguity about which method the system must implement.

FR-001 references a NIST Materials Data Repository DOI but the DOI is left blank ("DOI "). Without a concrete identifier the system cannot be verified to retrieve material properties, making the requirement untestable.

The ‘Verified Datasets’ block lists the OpenML URL as `https://www.openml.org/d/` with no dataset identifier, and FR-001 cites OpenML ID 42123. The missing identifier prevents any reviewer or test harness from locating the dataset, rendering related FRs and SCs unverifiable.

FR-011 requires validation against a “curated literature lookup table” that is never defined or provided in the spec. Without the table, the sign‑matching check cannot be performed, so the requirement is not verifiable.

FR-004 uses a Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) rule for outlier removal, whereas the idea specifies ±3 σ. This methodological change is not justified and drifts from the original research plan, potentially affecting reproducibility of results.

FR-011 requires validation of the sign of mean SHAP values against a curated literature lookup table. The original idea only demanded that SHAP direction match known physical trends; the lookup‑table requirement introduces a new validation step not requested.

SC-004 mandates that at least three features have statistically significant SHAP values (p < 0.05) based on a permutation‑test. The idea never called for significance testing of SHAP values, only for identifying a concise set of important descriptors. This adds an unrequested research question.
SC-005 imposes an execution‑time ceiling of ≤ 6 hours. The idea does not specify any runtime constraint; this is an engineering bound that was not part of the original scope.
SC-007 limits imputed material‑property rows to ≤ 5 % of the dataset. The original idea required median imputation but did not set a quantitative logging threshold, making this an over‑reach.
The NIST Materials Data Repository citation is missing its DOI (shown as empty parentheses). The idea explicitly references a NIST DOI; the spec fails to provide a verifiable external source.

The specification uses both `material_pair_id` (FR-014) and `pairing_id` (Edge Cases) to denote the grouping identifier. This inconsistency can cause traceability and data‑leakage issues, diverging from the clear terminology in the idea.

FR-014 mandates stratified splitting by `material_pair_id` only. If a single material appears in multiple pairings, that material can be present in both training and test sets, causing data leakage and potentially inflating R² scores. The split should also enforce that no individual material identifier appears in both sets (e.g., leave‑one‑material‑out or grouping on both constituent material IDs).

SC-004 requires at least three features to have mean absolute SHAP values that are statistically significant (p < 0.05) via a permutation‑test. SHAP values are derived from the fitted model; testing their significance on the same data used to train the model constitutes double‑dipping and does not provide a valid inference about true feature importance. A more appropriate approach would be to assess feature importance on held‑out data or via nested cross‑validation.

FR-004 uses a Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) rule for outlier removal, whereas the idea specifies ±3 σ. This methodological change is not justified and drifts from the original research plan, potentially affecting reproducibility of results.
